@texra-ai/harness/schemas ​

Browser-safe Effect Schemas, derived types, and pure read helpers for @texra-ai/harness.

Guide: Read Views, Transcripts & Renderers and Durable Protocol & Recovery for how views, runtime requests, and approval policies work.

  • Session & run views: SessionView, RunView, TranscriptView, PendingRequest, and pure queries (acceptsFollowUp, attentionOf, sessionActivity, descendantRuns, runActionRefusal).
  • Commands & approvals: RuntimeCommandSchema (RuntimeCommand), RequestDecision, OutcomeSchema, RequestErrorSchema, ApprovalPolicySchema, resolveBypass.
  • Agent definitions & run outcomes: AgentConfigSchema, InlinePersonaSchema, RunEndSchema, RunIdSchema, StartRequestSchema.
  • Settings & trace export: settingsCatalog, the harness's setting rows (SettingRow, each a StateKey), TraceDocumentSchema.

acceptsFollowUp ​

Whether a run takes a follow-up at all, the one rule every host reads (it decides whether the composer shows). A run launched taking none (takesFollowUps) and a run whose rows this build cannot read take none; a run still going or waiting takes one, as does a stopped root agent with saved steps, which a resume continues from its history.

ts
function acceptsFollowUp(run: ReadRunView): boolean

APPROVAL_POLICY_DEFAULT ​

ts
const APPROVAL_POLICY_DEFAULT: ApprovalPolicy

APPROVAL_POLICY_NO_INPUT_DEFAULT ​

The policy a --no-input run falls back to. Deliberately divergent from {@link APPROVAL_POLICY_DEFAULT}: a run that cannot present a prompt denies instead of hanging, and buildCliContext narrows the candidate list to the explicit --approval-policy flag alone — a persisted or env-provided yolo must not silently auto-approve a headless run that nobody is watching. Changing that requires changing headless discipline, not just this constant.

ts
const APPROVAL_POLICY_NO_INPUT_DEFAULT: ApprovalPolicy

APPROVAL_POLICY_SETTING ​

The approval policy. Strict on purpose: settingEnumOptions derives the dropdown from a literal-list row, and the tolerant spelling belongs to parseApprovalPolicy, which every reader of typed-in text (the env var, --approval-policy, /approval, the dropdown) calls before a value ever reaches this row.

ts
const APPROVAL_POLICY_SETTING: { readonly key: "approvalPolicy"; readonly slot: "config"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<Literals<readonly ["never", "ask", "yolo"]>, never>; readonly title: "Approval policy"; readonly description: "Whether agents ask before running shell commands and editing files."; readonly configTarget: "local"; readonly choices: { readonly never: { readonly label: "Block"; }; readonly ask: { readonly label: "Ask"; }; readonly yolo: { readonly label: "Auto-approve"; }; }; }

Attention ​

What wants this window: the requests it can answer (the badge), and since previous (none without it) the new ones and the runs that ended.

ts
interface Attention<Request> {
  readonly requests: readonly Request[];
  readonly arrived: readonly Request[];
  readonly finished: readonly ReadRunView[];
}

attentionOf ​

The one attention rule every host reads (the extension's badge, reveal and chime, the desktop's dock badge, notifications, and rail): a request wants the user when this window can answer it (not one on a run another process holds or waiting for its run's resume), and a run when its outcome lands.

ts
function attentionOf<View extends ReadSessionView>(
  view: View,
  previous?: ReadSessionView,
): Attention<View['requests'][number]>

blocksCaller ​

Whether a request blocks the tool that opened it: every kind the harness opens does, and a plugin's request as it declares. One that does not leaves its run working; its plugin's decision hook delivers the answer to whichever process holds the run by then, so it stays open across every resume. The folds and the decision door all read this one predicate.

Cancelled ​

Nothing is left to tell the user: they cancelled the operation, or the host has already told them why it did not go through. No refusal notice is needed.

ts
class Cancelled extends Schema.TaggedError<Cancelled>()(
  'Cancelled',
  {},
)

causeChain ​

err followed by its cause chain, outermost first; a Cause reads as the error it raised; an AggregateError's errors follow it before its cause, and an error whose reason carries the cause (a PlatformError, a SqlError) is followed by that cause. Shared traversal for messages and for predicates whose fact may sit at any depth of a wrapped error.

ts
function causeChain(err: unknown): unknown[]

CHATGPT_CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW_SETTING ​

The ChatGPT-subscription input budget; unset, each model takes the window the Codex backend grants it.

The stored unit is thousands of tokens, and the key says so. Every budget in play is a round multiple of 1000 (272K, 400K, 872K), so a raw token count is three zeros nobody wants to type and an off-by-1000 typo lands inside the valid range instead of being rejected: 872 entered for 872,000 is a legal 872-token budget that puts every request over the limit, and the failure then names a number the user never meant to set.

ts
const CHATGPT_CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW_SETTING: { readonly key: "chatgptCodex.contextWindowK"; readonly slot: "config"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<NullOr<Int>, never>; readonly title: "Subscription input token budget (K tokens)"; readonly description: "Input token budget for ChatGPT-subscription (Codex) routing, in thousands of tokens, mirroring Codex CLI's model_context_window. Unset, each model takes the window the Codex backend grants it; a value overrides it for every model, up to 872 (872,000 tokens). Automatic compaction may run earlier according to the separate compaction threshold. The model's output budget is added when displaying the total context window. The OpenAI backend enforces the real per-account limit — values above what your subscription allows fail and trigger compaction recovery."; }

CHATGPT_PREFER_SUBSCRIPTION_SETTING ​

ts
const CHATGPT_PREFER_SUBSCRIPTION_SETTING: { readonly key: "chatgptCodex.preferSubscription"; readonly slot: "config"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<Boolean, never>; readonly title: "Prefer the ChatGPT subscription"; readonly description: "Prefer your signed-in ChatGPT subscription for Codex-eligible OpenAI models instead of API-key routing. Experimental. Subscription routing takes the input window the Codex backend grants each model; use chatgptCodex.contextWindowK to override it."; }

ConfigTarget ​

Where a config write lands. workspace is the project's committable .texra/config.json, which a cloned repository controls; local is this user's private file for the workspace, under the storage root and never in the project; global is the user's file for every workspace.

countLines ​

Count the number of lines in a string. Handles both Unix (\n) and Windows (\r\n) line endings. A trailing newline does not count as an extra line.

  • @example countLines('a\nb\nc') // 3 countLines('a\nb\nc\n') // 3 (trailing newline ignored) countLines('') // 0
ts
function countLines(text: string): number

CredentialSwitchSchema ​

The move onto the user's own credential that a failed model request offers. It comes with the run's recorded failure, decided once from that failure and the route the model was bound on; hosts render it and never re-derive it from the error.

DEBUG_MODE_SETTING ​

Transcript verbosity, its one meaning: the debug tier of the transcript view and the detail of the payloads it shows. A log surface's own level filter decides what that surface prints, so no producer reads this row to widen or narrow a log; only a view build does.

ts
const DEBUG_MODE_SETTING: { readonly key: "logger.debugMode"; readonly slot: "config"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<Boolean, never>; readonly title: "Verbose transcript"; readonly description: "Show the transcript's verbose tier: debug-level rows and their payload detail. The log surfaces filter themselves (the Output view's own level filter, the desktop log file, the CLI's --verbose/--quiet)."; }

DeclinableUsageRoute ​

ts
type DeclinableUsageRoute = typeof DeclinableUsageRouteSchema.Type;

DeclinableUsageRouteSchema ​

The subscription routes a run can decline: storage's spelling of llm's PLAN_ROUTES, which the route decision converts both ways, so a plan in one list only fails to compile. A retry the user answered with their own API key declines the route that ran out of quota, for that run only: the choice is a fact of the run, not of the user's settings, so no preference is rewritten and two concurrent runs cannot cancel each other's fallback.

ts
const DeclinableUsageRouteSchema: Literals<readonly ["chatgpt-subscription", "xai-subscription", "kimi-code-subscription", "glm-coding-plan-subscription"]>

descendantRuns ​

Every run under rootRunId, parents first: the topology childIds (root to leaf) and ancestors (leaf to root) already state on every row, so a host walks the view's own facts instead of re-deriving them.

ts
function descendantRuns(
  view: Pick<ReadSessionView, 'runs'>,
  rootRunId: RunId | undefined,
  { includeRoot }: { includeRoot: boolean },
): readonly RunId[]

{@link FactNameSchema}'s value.

ts
type FactName = typeof FactNameSchema.Type;

FileListEntry ​

ts
type FileListEntry = typeof FileListEntrySchema.Type;

FileLocation ​

ts
type FileLocation = typeof FileLocationSchema.Type;

fileLocationAddressPath ​

How a location is addressed in text that leaves the UI — copied run context, follow-up prompts, subagent results. A run-storage location carries the run that owns it, so its /executions/... route resolves without the caller supplying one; every other kind reads as its display path.

ts
function fileLocationAddressPath(location: FileLocation): string

fileLocationDisplayPath ​

How a location reads as a path: workspace and run-storage files by their relative path — that is how the user and the agent's file tools refer to them — and external files by their absolute path, the only path they have.

This doubles as a location's comparable identity: two locations naming the same file agree here, so output-to-base maps key on it.

ts
function fileLocationDisplayPath(location: FileLocation): string

FileLocationSchema ​

Discriminated union of all file location types

ts
const FileLocationSchema: Union<readonly [Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"workspace">; readonly absolutePath: String; readonly relativePath: String; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"runStorage">; readonly absolutePath: String; readonly relativePath: String; readonly runId: brand<String, "RunId">; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"external">; readonly absolutePath: String; }>]>

fileLocationShortDisplayPath ​

Like {@link fileLocationDisplayPath} but collapses an external location to its basename, so a long absolute path (e.g. a run-storage file resolved as external because it sits outside the workspace root) cannot dominate a UI row or a prompt line. The full path stays on absolutePath.

ts
function fileLocationShortDisplayPath(location: FileLocation): string

FollowUpContent ​

ts
type FollowUpContent = typeof FollowUpContentSchema.Type;

FollowUpSender ​

ts
type FollowUpSender = typeof FollowUpSenderSchema.Type;

formatClippedList ​

The first max items of a list, then how many it leaves out (a, b, c +2 more), so every clipped list reads the same.

ts
function formatClippedList(
  items: readonly string[],
  max: number,
): string

formatCompactDuration ​

Compact duration capped at two units (45s, 3m 5s, 1h 1m).

Backed by pretty-ms with whole-second flooring, but renders zero / negative / sub-second durations as 0s (used by elapsed displays that start from zero, e.g. goal timings and server uptime).

ts
function formatCompactDuration(durationMs: number): string

formatCompactTokenCount ​

Format token counts for compact usage displays.

Token displays intentionally stay raw until they exceed 4096, the common small-context threshold where an abbreviated number starts buying space. Once k-format rounding would print 1000k, switch to M instead.

ts
function formatCompactTokenCount(tokens: number): string

formatCostUsd ​

Format a USD cost value as a display string with three decimal places. e.g. 0.012 → '$0.012'

ts
function formatCostUsd(cost: number): string

formatError ​

Format an error with a prefix for logging or user messages.

ts
function formatError(prefix: string, err: unknown): string

formatHunkLines ​

Hunks as unified-diff text lines, each preceded by its header. One header policy: a ,1 range is omitted, the form diff -u and git diff emit.

ts
function formatHunkLines(hunks: ToolEditContent['hunks']): string[]

formatResetDuration ​

A coarse wait (1d 20h, 20h 22m, 5m), as a used-up plan's reset is worded: two units at most, whole minutes, and no minutes once it reaches a day (pretty-ms would back-fill a zero hour with them, 1d 58m); under a minute is less than a minute.

ts
function formatResetDuration(durationMs: number): string

formatResultCount ​

Format a result count with proper pluralization. Example: formatResultCount(3, 'result') returns "3 results"

ts
function formatResultCount(
  count: number,
  singular: string,
  plural?: string,
): string

generateRunId ​

Mint a run id: 12 lowercase hex chars (48 bits of entropy), the first digits of a random UUID, every one of which is random. One of the two minting sites (deriveRunId is the other), so the brand is applied here and nowhere downstream. Any other random id is crypto.randomUUID().

ts
function generateRunId(): RunId

getBasename ​

Extract the base name (filename) from a file path. Handles platform-specific separators (\ on Windows, / on Unix).

  • @example getBasename('/home/user/document.pdf') // returns 'document.pdf' getBasename('C:\Users\file.txt') // returns 'file.txt' getBasename('/path/to/') // returns 'to' getBasename('/') // returns ''
ts
function getBasename(filePath: string | undefined | null): string

getFileStem ​

Basename without its final extension ('notes' for 'dir/notes.md'). Dotfiles keep their name ('.gitignore' → '.gitignore').

ts
function getFileStem(filePath: string | undefined | null): string

getModelLabel ​

Resolve a persisted model id to its static user-facing catalogue label.

ts
function getModelLabel(model: string): string

getProposalFileGroups ​

ts
function getProposalFileGroups(
  data: ProposalFileFields,
): ProposalFileGroup[]

The email beside {@link GIT_AUTHOR_NAME_SETTING}, by the same rule.

GIT_AUTHOR_NAME_SETTING ​

The identity agent-authored commits carry while commit marking is on. The harness names none: an app's catalog supplies its own (settingsCatalog's defaults), and while neither the person nor the app names one, commits keep git's own identity. .min(1) so a blank value is rejected at the write boundary.

const GIT_AUTHOR_NAME_SETTING: { readonly key: "git.authorName"; readonly slot: "repoState"; readonly schema: UndefinedOr<String>; readonly title: "Agent commit author"; readonly description: "Author and committer name used for agent-authored commits when commit marking is enabled."; }

Routes requests through the coding-specific endpoint with monthly quota limits."; }

Leave empty to use the default endpoint.`; readonly slot: "globalState"; }

GLM_REGION_SETTING ​

const GLM_REGION_SETTING: { readonly provider: "glm"; readonly key: "glm.useChina"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<Boolean, never>; readonly title: "GLM China region"; readonly description: "Use the China region endpoint instead of the international one. Enabled by default. API keys work with either endpoint."; readonly slot: "globalState"; }

GOAL_MAX_COST_SETTING ​

What a goal's rounds may spend before it pauses instead of starting another round; 0 disables the cap. Read when the goal launches, into its script. Global: a committed project config must not raise or remove the user's cap.

ts
const GOAL_MAX_COST_SETTING: { readonly key: "goal.maxCostUsd"; readonly slot: "config"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<Number, never>; readonly configTarget: "global"; readonly title: "Goal spend cap (USD)"; readonly description: "Spend in US dollars, across its rounds, at which an autonomous goal pauses instead of starting another round. Raise it, then run the goal again to continue. Set to 0 to remove the cap (not recommended with auto-approve on your own API key)."; }

GOAL_STRATEGY_SETTING ​

The script module whose goal export a plan run as a goal calls. The default is the goal plugin's own module; a scriptModules entry of any plugin that is on may replace it. Read when the goal launches. Global, as the cap is: the strategy is what checks the cap, so a committed project config must not pick one that ignores it.

ts
const GOAL_STRATEGY_SETTING: { readonly key: "goal.strategy"; readonly slot: "config"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<String, never>; readonly configTarget: "global"; readonly title: "Goal strategy"; readonly description: "The script module a plan run as a goal runs, by its import specifier (`builtIn:<module>`): its `goal(objective, { maxCostUsd })` export decides the rounds, what context each starts from and when to stop, and resolves to the goal's result. Defaults to the goal plugin's own module."; }

GoalResultSchema ​

A goal's result: what its strategy, the goal export of the script module the goal.strategy setting names, returns, and so the structured output its run ends with. completed when a round verified the objective, paused with the reason otherwise. A pause is a result, not a waiting run: work continues through a new goal or a new turn.

ts
const GoalResultSchema: Union<readonly [Struct<{ readonly rounds: Int; readonly spent: Finite; readonly report: String; readonly outcome: Literal<"completed">; }>, Struct<{ readonly rounds: Int; readonly spent: Finite; readonly report: String; readonly outcome: Literal<"paused">; readonly pause: Union<readonly [Struct<{ readonly reason: Literal<"needs_user">; }>, Struct<{ readonly reason: Literal<"round_failed">; readonly error: Struct<{ readonly name: String; readonly message: String; }>; }>, Struct<{ readonly reason: Literal<"no_verdict">; readonly response: String; }>, Struct<{ readonly reason: Literal<"spend_cap">; readonly maxCostUsd: Finite; }>]>; }>]>

const GOOGLE_BACKGROUND_RESPONSES_SETTING: { readonly key: "model.useGoogleBackgroundResponses"; readonly slot: "config"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<Boolean, never>; readonly configTarget: "global"; readonly title: "Google background responses"; readonly description: "Run text-only Google generations as background Interactions (submit + poll) instead of one long streamed request. Requires server-side conversation state and a model that supports background execution. Off by default; unsupported models fall back automatically."; }

GOOGLE_INTERACTIONS_SERVER_STATE_SETTING ​

Disable to keep conversations off Google's servers and resend the full transcript each round."; }

HARNESS_INSTRUCTION_KEY ​

The instruction keys the harness itself emits as {@link RequestShowInstructionPayload.key}. A key names the notice for the host's "never remind again" state; an embedder decides what each of these offers beside the message (TeXRA: the buttons that set a key or open a guide). An embedder's own notices use keys of their own.

InlinePersonaSchema ​

A persona an embedder passes inline (StartInput.agent) instead of a file: the same definition with nothing a file alone can mean. It has no bundled original and no plugin's block (a task is its plugin's recipe); each is refused as an unrecognized key.

ts
const InlinePersonaSchema: Struct<{ readonly description: optional<String>; readonly name: Trim; readonly prompt: optional<String>; readonly temperature: optional<Number>; readonly tools: optional<$Array<String>>; }>

InputHistoryRecord ​

ts
type InputHistoryRecord = typeof InputHistoryRecordSchema.Type;

InstalledPluginSchema ​

One installed plugin, persisted as a row of the plugins.installed state: the one install record every host reads and writes (a CLI's plugin command, a settings page). The plugin keeps its own manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json or .codex-plugin/plugin.json); this row is where it lives, whether it is enabled, the trust given to it, and what stands in for a manifest the plugin does not have (the marketplace entry's skill directories, version and description).

name takes the skill-name grammar, which also makes it a safe single path segment for the managed plugins/<name> directory. commit is set exactly when the harness fetched the plugin with git and owns its directory; a local plugin is referenced in place and has none.

ts
const InstalledPluginSchema: Struct<{ readonly name: decodeTo<String, String, never, never>; readonly source: String; readonly ref: optional<String>; readonly commit: optional<String>; readonly path: String; readonly skills: $Array<String>; readonly version: optional<String>; readonly description: optional<String>; readonly enabled: Boolean; readonly trust: optional<Struct<{ readonly version: NullOr<String>; readonly digest: String; }>>; }>

isModelOptionAvailable ​

Whether an option row can be run as shipped. Its availability was resolved when the options were read; this only reads that verdict.

ts
function isModelOptionAvailable(model: {
  readonly availability?: ModelAvailabilityKind;
}): boolean

isPackagedAgentSource ​

True for the sources whose definitions are read in place and are not the user's to edit: the bundled one, and an installed plugin's. Every surface that offers to open one presents it read-only and points edits at the custom copy; the extension additionally registers the bundled directories writable: false for its file tools.

ts
function isPackagedAgentSource(source: AgentSource): boolean

isPlainAgentIdentity ​

Whether an identity denotes a native agent rather than an external CLI.

ts
function isPlainAgentIdentity(
  identity: RunIdentity | null | undefined,
): boolean

isRunId ​

Whether a string is a run id, as {@link RunIdSchema} reads it.

ts
const isRunId: <I>(input: I) => input is I & string & Brand<"RunId">

isTaskConfig ​

Whether the run is a task (an agent carrying a plugin's block, run on its recipe): its value and its children's spend are its output, its end its record; it resumes from its checkpoint, its opening rebuilt. The app wrote its recipe, not a model, so the launch that chose the task granted it: tools fixed past any switch, the catalog's agents under the launch's approval, its prompts and files passed as written, and no skill activated by its instruction.

ts
const isTaskConfig: (config: { readonly name: string; readonly instruction: string; readonly workingDirectory?: string | undefined; readonly model?: string | undefined; } | { readonly agent: string; readonly model: string; readonly script?: { readonly kind: "background"; readonly title: string; readonly tools: readonly string[]; readonly code: string; readonly timeoutMs?: number | null | undefined; } | { readonly kind: "recipe"; readonly title: string; readonly tools: readonly string[]; readonly code: string; readonly block: string; readonly options: { readonly [x: string]: Json; }; readonly timeoutMs?: number | null | undefined; } | null | undefined; readonly workingDirectory?: string | null | undefined; readonly instruction?: string | undefined; readonly editedFile?: string | null | undefined; readonly inputFiles?: readonly string[] | undefined; readonly contextFiles?: readonly string[] | undefined; readonly mediaFiles?: readonly string[] | undefined; readonly outputFiles?: readonly string[] | undefined; readonly agentSource?: "plugin" | "custom" | "builtIn" | "inline" | null | undefined; readonly persona?: { readonly name: string; readonly description?: string | undefined; readonly prompt?: string | undefined; readonly tools?: readonly string[] | undefined; readonly temperature?: number | undefined; } | null | undefined; readonly asCaller?: boolean | null | undefined; readonly rootUserInstruction?: string | null | undefined; readonly displayInstruction?: string | null | undefined; readonly memories?: readonly string[] | undefined; readonly launch?: { readonly [x: string]: Json; } | null | undefined; readonly delegationAgentScope?: readonly string[] | null | undefined; readonly outputSchema?: { readonly [x: string]: unknown; } | null | undefined; }) => boolean

LaunchNoticeSchema ​

The notice a refused launch carries for its caller to show (LaunchRefused.notice), as the presentation event and payload a host's emit takes: the instruction for a model the build does not recognize, or the agent the launch named that the catalog does not hold. The launch shows nothing itself; the caller shows this where it shows the failure.

launchPolicy ​

The policy a launch's privileged actions (commands, edits, delegated work) are decided under: the project's, narrowed by the limit the launch asks for, or Auto-approve, which widens its own task but never over Block. Auto-approve gets there by turning the run's grants on (rootLaunch), not by changing the run's policy, which stays the project's: a question or a retry still goes to a person where one can answer it.

ts
function launchPolicy(
  project: ApprovalPolicy,
  approval: LaunchApproval | undefined,
): ApprovalPolicy

MODEL_AVAILABILITY_STATUS ​

What a kind means: whether a run can use the model (a surface's words for each kind are the app's). Declared once here, next to the kind, so the answer is carried on the wire as the kind alone and every host reads the same table instead of pre-fanned fields.

Written with as const satisfies so each available literal survives for computeModelOptions's derivation of the unavailable kinds, while a missing or misshapen kind is still a compile error, and frozen to the depth it is read at: the table crosses into every host that decides whether a model can run, and readonly is compile-time only.

ts
const MODEL_AVAILABILITY_STATUS: { readonly 'provider-key': { readonly available: true; }; readonly 'missing-key': { readonly available: false; }; readonly 'key-unreadable': { readonly available: false; }; readonly 'subscription-access': { readonly available: true; }; readonly retired: { readonly available: false; }; readonly unserved: { readonly available: false; }; readonly 'unknown-model': { readonly available: false; }; }

MODEL_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD_SETTING ​

The share of the model's context window that triggers automatic compaction; 0 disables it. No configTarget: both runtime readers resolve the merged config value through Settings.get, so narrowing the row to the global scope would hide (and block writes to) a workspace override the runtime honors.

ts
const MODEL_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD_SETTING: { readonly key: "model.compactionThresholdPercent"; readonly slot: "config"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<Number, never>; readonly title: "Compaction threshold"; readonly description: "When the conversation reaches this percentage of the model's context limit, earlier messages are summarized automatically to free up space. Lower values trigger summarization sooner. Set to 0 to disable."; }

MODEL_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS_SETTING ​

The number of automatic retries after the initial model request.

ts
const MODEL_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS_SETTING: { readonly key: "model.retry.maxAttempts"; readonly slot: "config"; readonly schema: withDecodingDefault<Int, never>; readonly title: "Automatic retries"; readonly description: "Additional automatic retries after the initial model request (0–5). A resumed request keeps the retries it already used."; }

QueuedFollowUp ​

A follow-up queued for the run and not yet consumed, as its row holds it.

ReadonlyDeep ​

A runtime value as a host or an embedder holds it: read-only all the way down, every map, array, and record included. The value itself is not copied (the fold publishes immutable levels); the type is what keeps a write from reaching it. A primitive stays itself, so a branded id (a RunId) is still that id.

ts
type ReadonlyDeep<T> = T extends
  | string
  | number
  | boolean
  | bigint
  | symbol
  | null
  | undefined
  | ((...args: never[]) => unknown)
  ? T
  : T extends ReadonlyMap<infer K, infer V>
    ? ReadonlyMap<K, ReadonlyDeep<V>>
    : T extends ReadonlySet<infer V>
      ? ReadonlySet<ReadonlyDeep<V>>
      : T extends readonly (infer E)[]
        ? readonly ReadonlyDeep<E>[]
        : T extends object
          ? { readonly [P in keyof T]: ReadonlyDeep<T[P]> }
          : T;

readTraceFacts ​

A parsed trace with each plugin fact checked as the store checks it, against the harness's built-in fact kind (the goal's plan) and the app's plugin fact kinds (appFactKinds). A fact at another version than its kind's, or whose value the kind's schema rejects, throws, naming it, as does a retired built-in fact no current plugin owns; one whose plugin this build lacks is kept as written, marked unavailable, as the store reads it.

ts
function readTraceFacts(
  document: TraceDocument,
  appFactKinds: readonly TraceFactKind[],
): TraceDocument

A cold read as the view's inputs, in the reader's order: the debug policy; the local snapshot, before the rows it describes (a run applied before it reads as held by nothing, and the transcript rows an unheld run finishes stay finished once it is known held); the listing; the subscription set; the subscribed aggregates' rows; and the marker. The live reader and an exported trace both answer a subscribe with it.

RequestAnswerability ​

Whether this window can answer a pending request: the one rule the host's attention badge and the request card both read, matching what SessionRequests.decide accepts. A request that blocks its caller is answered by the fiber waiting on it, so only while its run waits here; an interrupted run has to be resumed first. One that does not, at any time.

ts
type RequestAnswerability = 'answerable' | 'resume';

Who bypasses one kind's prompts for a run: the nearest run in its ancestry (itself first) that decides the kind, by its autonomous goal's grant (goal) or a human's value (human when on); null when nothing grants it. ResumeRefusalSchema ​

Why a persisted run is not continued here: the one answer a resume, a message to a run with no loop here, a run's records and its view give. finished (nothing left to continue from), blocked ({@link ResumeBlockedSchema}), unusableCheckpoint (its saved state is there but cannot be continued: never finished, which would say it ended normally), earlierBuild (an earlier build wrote its rows), pluginUnavailable (it holds a fact of plugin, which this process does not load, cause the fact's reason: it continues once a process loads it), or notResumable (it was deleted, or its input is closed).

rollupOf ​

What children and their descendants count toward a parent's rollup: the view's count over the run tree (each child's own rollup below it), and the dispatch card's over the tree it lists (below recurses through the children it lists instead). A child waiting between turns (held) or paused, nothing asked of the user, has delivered its turn: it counts as finished, not running.

  below = (child: ReadRunView) => child.rollup,

Canonical terminal outcome of an agent run — the single fact "how did this run end", decided exactly once at the run-lifecycle boundary. Current production writers use these values for terminal run, stage-end, and run state.

SessionRow ​

ts

SessionRowDraft ​

What a job appends (Append): the body plus the aggregate it lives on. The store stamps the rest of the envelope (seq, commit, at) as it appends; no caller passes them. Parsing a draft removes caller-supplied envelope fields before storage.

ts
type SessionRowDraft = typeof SessionRowDraftSchema.Type;

SessionStoreMovedAside ​

What opening a store moved aside, whole (never read again): a store written before 1.0, or a file SQLite reports damaged or not a database. Null when nothing was moved. The one fact a host presents about it.

  readonly path: string;
  readonly aside: string;
  readonly reason: 'pre-1.0' | 'corrupt';

SettingChoiceCopy ​

How a settings UI shows one value of an enum setting.

ts
interface SettingChoiceCopy {
  readonly label?: string;
  readonly description?: string;
}

SettingRow ​

One setting, whose schema decodes its stored value to an A.

ts
interface SettingRow<A = unknown> extends StateKey<A> {
  /** Short sentence-case label every settings UI shows for the row. */
  readonly title: string;
  /** Human-readable description, shared across every host that renders it. */
  readonly description: string;
  /** Config-backed target, workspace when omitted; `global`/`local` skip the project file. */
  readonly configTarget?: 'global' | 'workspace' | 'local';
  /**
   * A `global` row a project file may still switch off: its project value
   * counts unless it is `true`, so a repository can opt out (telemetry) but
   * never opt in. A malformed project value counts too, and fails closed.
   */
  readonly projectMayOptOut?: true;
  /**
   * Display copy for each value of an enum setting, keyed by the value, so
   * the record is total over the schema's values by type. The values
   * themselves are read off the schema, not restated here; a value without
   * a label shows as itself.
   */
  readonly choices?: { readonly [V in A & string]: SettingChoiceCopy };
}

settingsCatalog ​

The harness's rows, then rows (an app's own, its plugins' included), stored under namespace. A key declared twice is a defect and throws, and so does a defaults key that names no harness row.

ts
function settingsCatalog(options: {
  readonly namespace: string;
  readonly rows: readonly SettingRow[];
  /** The app's own defaults for harness rows, by key: the value an absent
   *  key reads as (the helper model, which the harness leaves unset). */
  readonly defaults?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  /** {@link SettingsCatalog.curatedModels}; none when absent. */
  readonly curatedModels?: readonly string[];
}): SettingsCatalog

SettingsCatalog ​

One settings catalog: its rows and the lookups the stores read from them.

ts
interface SettingsCatalog {
  /** The app's prefix on every stored key (`texra`): the config and state
   *  stores write a row's relative key as `<namespace>.<key>`. */
  readonly namespace: string;
  /** Every row, in catalog order. */
  readonly rows: readonly SettingRow[];
  /** Look up any row, config-file-backed or state-backed, by its key. */
  readonly byKey: (key: string) => SettingRow | undefined;
  /** Look up a row by its stored key, as a store lists it. */
  readonly byStoredKey: (storedKey: string) => SettingRow | undefined;
  /**
   * A fresh copy of a config-file-backed row's default, or `undefined` for a
   * key no such row owns: what every `ConfigProvider` answers for an absent
   * key. Parsed defaults are memoized
   * because this is on the read path of every absent setting; object values
   * are cloned so a caller cannot mutate the catalog's own default.
   */
  readonly configDefault: (key: string) => unknown;
  /** The models every user starts with enabled, in picker order; a person's
   *  selection is stored as a change over this list. The app's choice over
   *  the llm catalog: the harness curates none. */
  readonly curatedModels: readonly string[];
}

SettingStore ​

Storage slot a setting is read from / written to. repoState is shared by every checkout of one git repository (keyed by its root in the global database), so a repository has one value on every host and in every worktree.

ts
type SettingStore =
  | 'config'
  | 'workspaceState'
  | 'repoState'
  | 'globalState';

StateKey ​

One stored key: where it lives and what its stored value decodes to. A key that is not a setting (a stored record, a flag) is one of these beside its owner, read with Settings.state; a setting row is one with copy.

ts
interface StateKey<A = unknown> {
  /** The key, relative to its catalog's namespace (`memory.enabled`), which
   *  the stores add (`<namespace>.memory.enabled`). */
  readonly key: string;
  /** Where the value is stored, the same on every host. */
  readonly slot: SettingStore;
  /**
   * The schema, carrying validation, any bounds, and the decoding default
   * applied when the key is absent: decoding `undefined` yields that
   * default.
   */
  readonly schema: Schema.Codec<A, unknown>;
}

Normalize any thrown value into a user-friendly error message string: the error's own message, then the messages down its cause chain (and an AggregateError's members), each once, joined with : . A wrapper whose sentence already embeds its cause's message adds nothing, and a wrapper with a fixed sentence no longer hides the failure under it.

One finished run as a static viewer replays it: the run aggregate's own display events in commit order, the same rows the live plane delivers to a subscriber. Nothing is projected on the way out and nothing is reconstructed on the way in.

TraceFactKind ​

A plugin row kind as an imported trace reads it: a Plugin fact kind.

ts
interface TraceFactKind {
  readonly plugin: string;
  readonly kind: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly schema: Schema.Codec<unknown, unknown>;
}

TranscriptView ​

A stream's transcript slice: what hosts paint.

ts
type TranscriptView = RunView['transcript'];

truncateSummary ​

Collapse whitespace first, then truncate to a fixed-width one-line summary.

ts
function truncateSummary(text: string, maxLength: number): string

truncateWithEllipsis ​

Truncate a string to maxLen grapheme clusters with a trailing ellipsis (…). Returns the original string unchanged if it fits within the limit.

Uses Intl.Segmenter so multi-codepoint graphemes (ZWJ emoji sequences like 👨‍👩‍👧, combining diacritics, …) are counted and cut as single units — no split surrogates and no torn emoji.

  • @example truncateWithEllipsis('short', 60) // 'short' truncateWithEllipsis('a very long text', 10) // 'a very lo…'
ts
function truncateWithEllipsis(text: string, maxLen: number): string

Unavailable ​

The stream, request, or run the request names is gone or not in a state that can take it.

ts
class Unavailable extends Schema.TaggedError<Unavailable>()(
  'Unavailable',
  { runId: RunIdSchema, reason: Schema.String },
)

UnreadableRun ​

ts
type UnreadableRun = typeof UnreadableRunSchema.Type;

usageLimitMessage ​

A used-up plan in plain words, under the names its reader knows the plan and its fallback by: what ran out, when it resets, and what to do.

ts
function usageLimitMessage(
  used: UsedUpPlan,
  names: { readonly plan: string; readonly fallback: string },
): string

UsageRoute ​

The route a request's usage is billed through.

ts
type UsageRoute = typeof UsageRouteSchema.Type;

UsedUpPlan ​

A used-up plan as llm's verdict names it.

ts
type UsedUpPlan = {
  readonly plan: DeclinableUsageRoute;
  readonly planType?: string | undefined;
  readonly resetsInMs?: number | undefined;
};

usedUpPlanOf ​

The plan a failure says ran out, with its tier and reset; none for the account's own credit or any other failure.

ts
function usedUpPlanOf(failure: ModelFailure): UsedUpPlan | undefined
